question: At a PHC, three children with cough are assessed. Child A is 5 weeks old with RR 62/min. Child B is 9 months old with RR 52/min. Child C is 3 years old with RR 42/min. Based solely on fast-breathing thresholds in the IMNCI algorithm, which child (or children) meet the fast-breathing criterion for their age group?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Child A does meet the fast-breathing threshold for <2 months (≥60/min). However, Child B also meets the threshold — at 2–12 months, fast breathing is defined as ≥50/min (RR 52/min qualifies). Child C at 3 years has a threshold of ≥40/min, and RR 42/min also qualifies.

Child A (5 weeks, RR 62/min, threshold ≥60/min) and Child B (9 months, RR 52/min, threshold ≥50/min) both qualify. But Child C (3 years, RR 42/min) also meets the threshold for the 12 months–5 years group, which is ≥40/min.

answers.text: All three children (Child A, Child B, and Child C).

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. IMNCI fast-breathing thresholds: <2 months = ≥60/min (Child A: 62/min — YES); 2–12 months = ≥50/min (Child B: 52/min — YES); 12 months–5 years = ≥40/min (Child C: 42/min — YES). All three meet the criterion for their age band.
Child A at 5 weeks has a fast-breathing threshold of ≥60/min, and RR 62/min exceeds this. All three children meet the IMNCI fast-breathing criterion for their respective age groups.

overallFeedback.feedback: The three IMNCI fast-breathing thresholds are: <2 months ≥60/min; 2–12 months ≥50/min; 12 months–5 years ≥40/min. Apply each threshold to the correct age group — all three children in this question exceed their respective thresholds.

Memorise the three IMNCI fast-breathing thresholds: < 2 months ≥ 60/min; 2–12 months ≥ 50/min; 12 months–5 years ≥ 40/min. These age-specific cut-offs reflect developmental changes in basal respiratory rate and are essential for correct pneumonia classification.
